subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the Children of Echoes

755050101.text: Hey, Xilonen! Didn't expect to see you here.

755050102.text: Hey there, Traveler, Paimon! What, is it so weird to see me at my own home?

755050103.text: Well, no, but Paimon thought you'd have found a beautiful tree to get a few days' shut-eye in by now since we just solved such a big problem.

755050104.text: Haha, I'd love to, but everyone's been busy with the reconstruction. It'd feel wrong to slack off at a time like this.

755050105.text: So this is where you've decided to contribute?

755050106.text: Here, let me show you something.

755050112.text: This is a Phlogiston Honey Pearl with peculiar patterning that's been making the rounds recently in the market. They're usually produced by Phlogiston Aphids. Pretty common, really.

755050113.text: But these oddly patterned ones are both novel and scarce, making them quite expensive.

755050114.text: Paimon gets it! That's just like how we love treasure chests that have awesome-looking patterns on them too!

755050115.text: Hehe, so I bought a few for my collection, and guess what? After a few days, the potted plant I was raising nearby had withered.

755050116.text: I didn't think much of it at first. I mean, I don't know the first thing about growing plants anyway. Later, however, I heard Kachina say that some people got sick.

755050117.text: Most of them were customers of Cheven's gemstone shop. Even Cheven herself proved no exception.

755050118.text: Huh? Wait... Did it all have something to do with this gem, then?

755050119.text: I thought so too, and so I smashed one open... and discovered that it contained some Abyssal energy.

755050120.text: Low-concentration, of course, and isolated by the outer shell of the honey pearl itself — which made it almost undetectable.

755050121.text: What about the victims? How are they doing now?

755050122.text: No need to worry. The low concentration resulted in rather minor maladies, with most being sleepy or being prone to exhaustion.

755050123.text: It hasn't had any effect on the more fit, like myself or Kachina.

755050124.text: Phew... And here Paimon thought this might be a sticky situation.

755050125.text: Sticky? Like the honey in Honey Pearls?

755050126.text: I'd bet Paimon was thinking "sticky like Slimes" instead.

755050127.text: Hehe, you know it! And fortunately for us, this problem's only a threat to ordinary people, just like Slimes!

755050128.text: Heh, you two really understand one another.

755050129.text: We totally do! Still, we've met lots of people scared stiff by Slimes, so it's not like we can ignore it just because it isn't dangerous for us, right?

755050130.text: Exactly. I already explained the situation to our Chief, and asked him to collect and destroy all the strange Honey Pearls on the market.

755050131.text: But we still need to attack this issue at the source.

755050132.text: My sentiments exactly. Like I said, Phlogiston Honey Pearls are produced by Phlogiston Aphids. If anything is the source of the problem, it'll be them.

755050133.text: I went to look for Kinich, since he's got the better head for investigating between us. Yesterday, he sent word that he found Aphids with Abyssal contamination.

755050134.text: There are also traces of their presence near the Scions of the Canopy and the People of the Springs. Right, and Kinich also notified Mualani.

755050135.text: However, they're not exactly gemstone enthusiasts, so the problem didn't affect them as much.

755050136.text: Hmm... Looks like there are all sorts of lingering Abyss-related issues, huh? Guess we've gotta be patient.

755050137.text: How do you plan to deal with the Aphids?

755050138.text: Catch 'em first. We can still purify this level of Abyssal contamination, we shouldn't need to harm the Aphids.

755050139.text: Kinich has marked out places where they gather, and I'm heading to a spot near our tribe.

755050140.text: Would you like to come along, by the way? A little bug-catching sounds like fun, doesn't it?

755050141.text: I'd have invited Kachina, but unfortunately, she's already occupied.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to where the Abyssal Aphids were spotted

755050202.text: See that? An Aphid, polluted with the power of the Abyss. Way larger than any normal one ever gets.

755050203.text: Whoa, what a huge Aphid... Uh, is it dangerous?

755050204.text: Relax, even though it's been contaminated by the Abyss, its behavior doesn't seem to have changed at all.

755050205.text: Still, I've specially prepared an extra-large insect net to make sure everything goes smoothly. Here ya go. It'll come in handy for catching them in a moment.

755050206.text: Oh right! By the way, Kinich mentioned something rather unusual. He discovered that there's a special berry that always grows near areas where Abyssal Aphids are found.

755050207.text: The berry contains a toxin that can paralyze the Aphids, so if we spread them on the net, it'll stop the Aphids from struggling.

755050208.text: Huh? Why are Aphids living around a berry that paralyzes them? Seems kinda strange to Paimon...

755050209.text: I think so too. First time I've heard of animals living alongside something that's dangerous to them.

755050210.text: It's totally unnatural! Wait... Could someone be behind them getting infected with the Abyss!?

755050211.text: Paimon's sure on high alert these days.

755050212.text: Hey! Even the dumbest guides grow up! And Paimon was never dumb to start with anyway.

755050213.text: The only problem with that is that we searched everywhere, but didn't find any trace of human involvement.

755050214.text: So let's just chalk it up to some unknown natural Aphid behavior for now.

755050215.text: Fine, but no matter what, we've got to catch them first! We don't want anything else that makes people sick running around.

755050301.text: Phew! We did it! Though this bugger certainly looks big, it was pretty easy to catch.

755050302.text: It's not dangerous at all, other than the fact it likes to run away. The insect net and numbing berries were really useful too!

755050303.text: Hehe, but seeing as that it's the Abyss these Aphids are contaminated with, they could attract monsters. Best to be on your guard.

755050304.text: Yeah, you're right! And since these all-too-convenient berries just happen to be here... Well, if it was Paimon, she'd steer clear of any enemies!

755050305.text: #Being around berries like this isn't normal or natural, {NICKNAME}! We should keep our eyes peeled. There's something real fishy going on for sure!

755050306.text: You certainly look like an expert on suspicious goings-on.

755050307.text: Hehe, Paimon learned it from you!

755050309.text: Anyway, thanks for coming out here with me. We've taken care of one area, so it's about time for a nice little break.

755050310.text: After all, I'll need your help over the next few days too.
